methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring

data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ stage semiconductor company that has raised $236M to date, including a $36M strategic investment grant in August 2025. The target operates within a competitive landscape of 13 same-sector peers, though the private frontier-chip segment remains fragmented. Public comparables in Semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trade at a median 20.4x price-to-sales, while relevant private peers include Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Two standard valuation approaches prove inapplicable here. Peer-median triangulation fails due to insufficient datapoints: while 13 same-sector peers exist, no subset of three or more companies meets filters for identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. Public-comp anchoring cannot proceed without the target's disclosed revenue, which private companies typically withhold. The public semiconductor median of 20.4x P/S offers directional context only but remains non-binding absent revenue disclosure.

The analysis therefore supports no quantitative valuation range at this stage. Key uncertainties preventing closure include: (1) lack of revenue or comparable revenue multiples within Ranovus's narrow private peer cohort, (2) absence of sufficient same-stage private comps with disclosed valuations, and (3) inapplicability of public multiples without revenue normalization. A defensible valuation would require either target revenue disclosure or access to pricing data from recent raises by direct competitors at similar stages.
